Component: Main app: Staff Monitor table, Dashboard/floor map/mini list (state-management / display)
Reproduction: Live Demo > Start Manual Demo > at ~2 s choose "Sudden communication loss" > Inject fault > wait ~6 s (sensor DISCONNECTED, 6 min unmonitored) > open Staff Monitor and Dashboard. (Scripted: ui_audit.py section "outage-main-views")
Expected: Worker ST-02 shown as UNKNOWN / MONITORING UNAVAILABLE and today dose flagged incomplete on every RSO surface (approved Phase-3 requirement: UNKNOWN worker status; observed dose never presented as complete)
Actual: Staff Monitor row: "ST-02 ... 0.30 mSv 9.8 mSv NORMAL". Dashboard/floor map: no mention of unavailable monitoring. Correct UNKNOWN / HISTORICAL / incomplete-dose display exists only in the Live Demo panel, the smartwatch face ("NO CURRENT DATA"), the Wearable page and as a DATA QUALITY alert + toast. staff record: status "normal", dataStatus "unknown" (dataStatus is read only by Live Demo and watch code)
Evidence: logs/ui_audit_results.json (area outage-main-views, 3 FAIL); screenshots/04c_staff_monitor_during_outage.png, 04d_dashboard_during_outage.png, 04_disconnect_during_active_incident_unknown_state.png (correct Live Demo panel for contrast)
Impact: Operational/safety-presentation: an RSO using the Staff Monitor/Dashboard sees a normal-looking worker whose sensor is disconnected; contradicts the Phase-3 claim that unusable data is never shown as NORMAL. Mitigations that exist: DATA QUALITY alert and toast, Wearable page NO CURRENT DATA. Note: the Staff Monitor badge is documented on-page as a cumulative-dose warning level, but the dose total is also unmarked. Strictest reading of "conceals unavailable monitoring" would make this a BLOCKER.
Minimal_correction: Display-only: in renderStaff / renderFloorMap / renderStaffMiniList read staff.dataStatus and show a badge "UNKNOWN - MONITORING UNAVAILABLE" (or "DATA UNCERTAIN") and an "incomplete - N min unmonitored" note beside the dose. No change to detection logic, thresholds or dose arithmetic.
Retest_status: VERIFIED — tests T-H01 (20), UI audit, before/after screenshots

Reproduction: Run t_validation.py (original) against the Phase-3 build: it reports 1 failed; echo $? -> 0. Same for 5 mutant builds with 1-12 failures each.
Expected: Runner exits non-zero when any assertion fails (audit requirement 10)
Actual: No suite calls sys.exit on failure; exit code is 0 unless an exception crashes the script. t_validation.py: 113 passed, 1 failed, exit_code=0; mutants m1-m5: 1,12,6,5,3 failures, exit_code=0
Impact: CI or a reader trusting the exit code would report green on a failing suite. Pass/fail is only visible in the printed summary.
Minimal_correction: Append sys.exit(1 if any FAIL else 0) to each suite (tests only, no assertion change).
Retest_status: VERIFIED — runners exit 1 on failure (t_validation.py exit 1; baseline run of t_final_fixes exit 1)

Reproduction: Start Manual Demo, wait 12 s (scripted stream of 10 minutes has ended), choose "Sudden communication loss", Inject fault, wait 3.5 s.
Expected: Control disabled/explained, or sensor state changes
Actual: State stays "Sensor state: HEALTHY (fault active: disconnect)"; the timer is stopped, no samples arrive, no message. Also the scripted stream is only 10 simulated minutes (14 if the worker acknowledges), so a late injection can never reach DISCONNECTED/recovery on screen.
Evidence: logs/ui_audit_results.json (live demo, fault after stream end); screenshots/06b_live_demo_fault_after_stream_end_inert.png
Impact: Presentation: a stale HEALTHY badge beside "fault active" is confusing and contradicts the no-stale-as-current principle; presenter must inject within the first ~8 s.
Minimal_correction: Disable the fault controls (with a one-line hint) when no stream is running, and document the injection window in the demo script.
